newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan details Japan-U.S. insurance note.
newsitem.headline: Japan details Japan-U.S. insurance note.

text.p: Japanese firms will be allowed to enter the so-called "third-sector" insurance market if a dispute with the United States is not solved by the December 15 deadline, Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Wednesday.

"Japan and the U.S. signed a memorandum which confirms that conditions which we set on the entry into the third sector market will be no longer valid if we fail to reach an accord," Kubo told a late-night news conference.
Under the conditions, subsidiaries of Japanese non-life insurers will be barred from selling stand-alone cancer, hospitalisation and nursing care policies before January 1, 1997.
Subsidiaries of life insurance firms will not be allowed to offer personal accident insurance also before January 1.

Kubo said those conditions could be revised if they reach an agreement, pointing to a possibility that the entry by Japanese firms into the third-sector market in which foreign insurers have a stronghold will be further delayed.

"When the insurance talks reach an amicable and timely conclusion that is consistent with Japanese laws and regulations, MOF will change as necessary the license conditions in order to implement the result of the talks," the memorandum said.
At issue is Japan's $382 billion domestic insurance market.
The United States is pressing Japan to open its primary insurance markets but wants the "third sector" from being opened to Japanese insurers in the interim.
The dispute has become a major trade irritant between the two countries. They had originally set a July 31 deadline to settle the dispute but agreed this week to push that to December 15.
